HomePage.title: OAuth and OIDC Playground
HomePage.description: Explore OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect flows end-to-end with a guided, step-by-step experience. Choose an Entra or Auth0 workspace, configure app settings, generate authorization URLs, and walk through PKCE creation, callbacks, and token exchanges. See the exact requests and responses at each stage, decode and validate tokens, and understand key claims and security checks.

entra.title: Microsoft Entra ID workspace
entra.description: Walk through OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect flows against a Microsoft Entra ID tenant. Settings in this workspace are tenant-centric and are stored separately from the Auth0 workspace.

auth0.title: Auth0 workspace
auth0.description: Walk through OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect flows against an Auth0 tenant. Settings in this workspace are issuer- and audience-centric, and the authorization code flows add Auth0 options such as RAR, PAR and JAR.

ToolsJwtDecoder.title: JWT Decoder
ToolsJwtDecoder.description: Paste a JWT or compact JWE and inspect its protected header and any readable payload claims.

help.jwt: Paste a full JWT or compact JWE from another source. A leading 'Bearer ' prefix is ignored.
help.payloadClaims: Decoded JSON payload claims when available. Encrypted JWE payloads cannot be decoded client-side.

authorize.description: We build the authorization URL including your client_id, redirect_uri, scopes, optional state and nonce, and PKCE parameters. Depending on the provider, you can also set prompt behavior, login hints, response handling, and other provider-specific authorization parameters before opening the popup. After completing sign-in, the popup will redirect back and the callback step will auto-fill with the returned values.

settings.userProvidedDescription: These fields are configured by you and are used to build the authorization request.

par.title: Pushed Authorization Request (PAR - RFC 9126)
par.description: Push authorization parameters over a backchannel HTTP POST before launching the browser. Auth0 returns a request_uri which is then used on the authorization endpoint.

help.responseType: OAuth response_type parameter; for PKCE it is 'code'.
help.state: Opaque value to maintain state between request and callback; helps prevent CSRF.
help.nonce: A string to associate a client session with an ID token; helps mitigate replay attacks.
help.responseMode: Where the response should be returned (query or form_post).
help.prompt: Controls interactive behavior, for example login, consent, none, or provider-specific prompt values.
help.loginHint: Prefill the username or sign-in hint (e.g., email).
help.authUrlPreview: The full authorization URL that will open in the popup.
help.parEndpoint: The endpoint where authorization parameters are pushed via backchannel HTTP POST.
help.parRequest: Parameters that are pushed to the PAR endpoint, including client credentials, scopes, and authorization_details.
help.parResponse: Live response returned by the PAR endpoint containing the request_uri and expires_in.
help.browserAuthUrl: The clean authorization URL referencing the request_uri, which opens in the browser popup.

callApi.description: Call a protected API with the access token. Adjust the endpoint and send the GET request to see the response.

help.apiEndpoint: HTTP endpoint to call with the access token (for example, Microsoft Graph or an OIDC userinfo endpoint).
help.apiHeaders: HTTP headers used for the API call (includes Authorization).
help.apiResponse: Raw response from the API call (pretty-printed if JSON).

modeDescriptions.url: Send the authorization request directly on the browser URL.
modeDescriptions.par: Push the same authorization parameters to Auth0 first, then launch the browser with a request_uri.
modeDescriptions.jar: Sign the same authorization parameters into a request object and send that object on the authorize URL. A runtime private key is required.
modeDescriptions.parJar: Sign the authorization parameters into a request object, push it to Auth0, and launch with a request_uri. A runtime private key is required.

help.mode: Auth0 authorization request transport: plain URL, pushed authorization request (PAR), JWT-secured authorization request (JAR), or PAR with a request object.
help.clientAuthMethod: Choose how the client authenticates when pushing the authorization request to Auth0's PAR endpoint.
help.connection: Optional Auth0 connection name to preselect a specific identity provider or database connection.
help.connectionScope: Optional connection-specific scopes for supported upstream identity providers.
help.organization: Optional Auth0 organization identifier or name for organization-aware login flows.
help.invitation: Optional invitation identifier used together with organization invitations.
help.screenHint: Optional hint for the Universal Login experience, for example starting on signup.
help.maxAge: Maximum acceptable time in seconds since the user's last authentication.
help.uiLocales: Ordered space-separated list of UI locales to request from the login experience.
help.acrValues: Optional space-separated Authentication Context Class Reference values.
help.claimsLocales: Ordered space-separated list of locales for claim values.
help.idTokenHint: Previously issued ID token hint when the authorization request needs end-user context.
help.rarJson: Optional Rich Authorization Requests JSON. Auth0 sends this as authorization_details.
help.clientSecret: The pushed authorization request is itself an authenticated call to Auth0, so the secret is needed here rather than at the later client authentication step. It is the same value that step uses, so entering it once is enough.
help.requestObjectKey: PKCS#8 PEM private key used to sign the request object. It stays in memory for this session and is never persisted. The same key is reused if you later choose private_key_jwt for client authentication.
help.requestObjectKid: Identifies which registered key signed the request object. For Auth0 this is the key ID of the application credential holding the matching public key.
help.privateKey: Keep this secure! PKCS#8 PEM private key used to sign the client assertion for PAR. It stays in memory for this session and is never persisted.
help.clientAssertionKid: This should match the key identifier configured for the client signing key at Auth0.
help.dpopJkt: RFC 9449 SHA-256 thumbprint of the client's DPoP public key. Binds the authorization code to this specific key pair.

placeholders.requestObjectKid: Key ID of the registered signing key
placeholders.clientAssertionKid: Key ID of the registered signing key

errors.parMissingRequestUri: PAR response did not include a request_uri.
errors.requestObjectMissingPrivateKey: JAR requires a runtime private key. Generate or paste one before launching.
errors.requestObjectMissing: Request object response did not include a request value.
errors.rarInvalidJson: Authorization details must be valid JSON.
errors.rarNotArray: Authorization details must be a JSON array of objects.
errors.rarEmptyArray: Authorization details must contain at least one entry.
errors.rarEntryNotObject: Every authorization details entry must be a JSON object.
errors.rarEntryMissingType: Every authorization details entry needs a non-empty "type" string.
errors.rarTooLarge: Authorization details must stay under {max} characters.

callback.description: Inspect the callback URL or POST body for the authorization code, state, or any returned errors after sign-in.

help.callbackUrl: The full callback URL captured from the popup after sign-in.
help.callbackBody: If response_mode=form_post, the identity provider sends parameters in the POST body.
help.extractedCode: The authorization code extracted from the callback parameters.
help.extractedState: The state value extracted from the callback parameters (if set).
help.error: Short error code returned by the authorization server (the 'error' parameter).
help.errorUri: Optional URI with more information about the error (the 'error_uri' parameter).
help.errorDescription: Optional human-readable description of the error (the 'error_description' parameter).

pkce.description: PKCE secures public clients. Click the Generate button (left of the Code Verifier input) to create a high-entropy code_verifier and its code_challenge (S256 by default).

help.codeVerifier: High-entropy random string kept secret by the client (PKCE).
help.codeChallenge: Base64url-encoded SHA-256 hash of the code_verifier (S256).

blocked.providerConfig: The provider is not configured yet. Go back to Settings and fill in the tenant or issuer.
blocked.clientId: No client ID. Go back to Settings and enter the one from your application registration.
blocked.redirectUri: No redirect URI. Go back to Settings and set the one registered with the application.
blocked.tokenEndpoint: The token endpoint could not be resolved. Check the issuer in Settings, or set an endpoint override.
blocked.grantParameters: This grant needs an API audience (Auth0) or scopes (Entra). Go back to Settings and set one.
blocked.authCode: No authorization code. Run the Authorize step and complete the sign-in first.
blocked.codeVerifier: No PKCE code verifier. Go back to the PKCE step and generate one.
blocked.clientSecret: No client secret. Go back to the Client authentication step and enter it.
blocked.privateKey: No private key. Go back to the Client authentication step and supply the key that signs the client assertion.

tokens.description: Request tokens from the token endpoint and inspect both the request and response.

help.tokenEndpointPreview: The full token endpoint URL that will be used to exchange the authorization code.
help.tokenRequest: The POST body (x-www-form-urlencoded) used to exchange the code for tokens.

dpop.proofHelp: RFC 9449 proof-of-possession JWT signed with ES256 and sent in the 'DPoP' HTTP request header.
dpop.proofPending: A fresh DPoP Proof JWT will be signed with ES256 and sent in the 'DPoP' header when sending this token request.
dpop.tokenTypeHelp: Auth0 confirmed proof-of-possession binding by returning token_type: DPoP.
dpop.nonceRetriedNotice: Auth0 challenged with error 'use_dpop_nonce'. The request was automatically retried with the fresh 'DPoP-Nonce' header provided by the server.

validate.title: Validate tokens
validate.description: This guide walks through how to validate the ID and access tokens you received: first, how signature validation works (kid -> metadata -> jwks -> verify), then the common claim checks you should perform (aud, iss, tid, nonce, scopes/roles, exp, nbf, iat).

validateUi.graphWarning: Access tokens for Microsoft Graph (aud {aud}) typically cannot be signature-validated by this client. Only Microsoft Graph can validate their signatures.
validateUi.encryptedAccessToken: This access token is an encrypted JWE. Only the protected header is readable here; signature validation must happen wherever the token can be decrypted.
validateUi.encryptedIdToken: This ID token is an encrypted JWE. Only the protected header is readable here; the client that holds the decryption key verifies the signature after decrypting it.
validateUi.opaqueAccessToken: This access token is opaque, not a JWT. Auth0 issues an opaque token when the authorization request names no API audience. It is a bearer credential the authorization server looks up on its own, so there is no signature for a client to check.
validateUi.opaqueClaimValidation: An opaque token carries no claims. The authorization server resolves it at its userinfo or introspection endpoint; a client validates nothing locally.
validateUi.encryptedClaimValidation: Claim validation is skipped because the encrypted payload is not available in the browser.

id.exp: exp must be in the future
id.nbfIat: nbf/iat must be <= now (with small skew)

access.exp: exp must be in the future
access.nbfIat: nbf/iat must be <= now (with small skew)
access.msGraph: (Microsoft Graph audience; only Graph can verify signatures)

settings.description: Configure your provider and client settings for this flow.
settings.userProvidedDescription: These fields are configurable by you and are used to build the authorization request.
settings.localStorageNotice: These values will be saved in your browser's local storage for convenience.
settings.resolvedDescription: These values are derived from the provider and other inputs. Enable endpoint overrides to edit them.

help.tenantId: Directory (tenant) GUID of your Entra ID instance.
help.issuerUrl: HTTPS issuer URL from your Auth0 tenant. Discovery uses issuer/.well-known/openid-configuration.
help.clientId: Application client ID from your provider registration.
help.scopes: Space-separated scopes to request (e.g., openid profile offline_access api://.../scope.read).
help.audience: Optional API audience. Auth0 commonly requires this for API access and client credentials tokens.
help.authEndpoint: Authorization endpoint resolved from the selected provider or OIDC discovery metadata.
help.tokenEndpoint: Token endpoint resolved from the selected provider or OIDC discovery metadata.
help.redirectUri: Callback URL for this app. Must match the redirect URI in the app registration.
help.streamlined: Automatically runs steps and hides advanced fields to speed up the demo.
help.pkceEnabled: PKCE is recommended for public clients and optional for confidential clients.
help.dpopEnabled: Demonstrating Proof-of-Possession binds issued tokens and authorization codes to an asymmetric key pair held by the browser, preventing token replay attacks.
help.endpointOverride: Use custom authorization or token endpoints instead of the provider defaults or discovered metadata. Server-side token exchange still validates the endpoint.

errors.tenantIdInvalid: Tenant is required and must be a GUID
errors.issuerUrlInvalid: Issuer URL must be a valid HTTPS Auth0 tenant issuer URL
errors.discoveryFailed: Could not load OIDC discovery metadata: {error}
errors.clientIdRequired: Client ID is required and must be a GUID
errors.clientIdInvalid: Client ID must be a GUID
errors.redirectUriInvalid: Redirect URI must be a valid http(s) URL

decode.description: Access and ID tokens are often JWTs, but some providers return encrypted JWE tokens. Click 'Decode' to inspect the protected header and any readable payload claims.

help.accessToken: Access token to call APIs. Depending on the provider, this may be a signed JWT or an encrypted JWE.
help.idToken: ID token representing the user identity. Typically a signed JWT.
help.accessHeader: Decoded JOSE protected header of the access token.
help.accessPayload: Decoded JSON payload of the access token when available. Encrypted JWE payloads are not readable client-side.
help.idHeader: Decoded JOSE protected header of the ID token.
help.idPayload: Decoded JSON payload of the ID token when available. Encrypted JWE payloads are not readable client-side.

notes.accessHeaderNonce: This access token header contains a nonce field. This is a provider-specific JOSE header and is unrelated to the OIDC nonce claim, which is validated in the ID token payload.
notes.encryptedToken: This token is an encrypted JWE. The protected header can be shown, but the payload cannot be decoded in the browser without the decryption key.
notes.opaqueToken: This access token is opaque rather than a JWT, which is what Auth0 returns when the authorization request names no API audience. There is nothing inside to decode: the token is a reference the authorization server resolves itself. Set an API audience in Settings to receive a JWT instead.

claimsDialog.noClaims: No claims available. Decode the token payload first.
claimsDialog.unknownClaimDescription: Likely a custom or currently undocumented claim.
claimsDialog.namespacedClaimDescription: Custom namespaced claim added by the tenant, for example through an Auth0 action or an Entra claims mapping policy. Namespaced claims are not part of the registered JWT claim set.

common.aud: Audience: identifies the intended recipient of the token.
common.iss: Issuer: the security token service that issued the token.
common.iat: Issued at: the time when the token was issued.
common.nbf: Not before: earliest time the token is valid.
common.exp: Expiration time: latest time the token is valid.
common.sub: Subject: stable identifier for the authenticated principal.
common.jti: JWT ID: unique identifier for this token, usable for replay detection.
common.nonce: Nonce from the original auth request, used to mitigate replay in ID tokens.
common.at_hash: Access token hash tied to the ID token in hybrid/auth flows.
common.c_hash: Authorization code hash tied to the ID token in hybrid flows.
common.azp: Authorized party: application allowed to use this token.
common.preferred_username: Preferred username display value, often suitable as sign-in hint.
common.name: Human-readable display name for the user.
common.email: Email address claim when configured and available.
common.email_verified: Whether the email address has been verified by the provider.
common.given_name: Given name (first name) of the user.
common.family_name: Family name (last name) of the user.
common.nickname: Casual name for the user, may or may not be unique.
common.picture: URL of a profile picture for the user.
common.locale: Preferred locale of the user, for example en-US.
common.updated_at: Time the user profile was last updated.
common.amr: Authentication method references used during sign-in.
common.sid: Session identifier for sign-in session tracking.
common.cnf: Confirmation — identifies the proof-of-possession key bound to this token (RFC 7800 / RFC 9449).
common.cnf.jkt: JWK SHA-256 Thumbprint of the DPoP public key bound to this token.

entra.tid: Tenant ID: Microsoft Entra tenant GUID.
entra.aio: Internal claim used by Microsoft Entra for token reuse/telemetry semantics.
entra.azpacr: How the authorized party authenticated (for example public vs confidential).
entra.appid: Application ID of the client or calling app.
entra.appidacr: Authentication context class for the app identity.
entra.idp: Identity provider that authenticated the user.
entra.oid: Object ID of the user or service principal in the tenant.
entra.ipaddr: IP address of the client at authentication time.
entra.onprem_sid: On-premises SID when synchronized from Active Directory.
entra.pwd_url: URL where the user can change/reset password.
entra.rh: Refresh token/session binding hint used by Microsoft identity platform.
entra.scp: Scopes granted to the client for delegated access.
entra.roles: App roles or application permissions granted in the token.
entra.wids: Tenant-wide role template IDs assigned to the principal.
entra.groups: Security groups claim (may be omitted or overage-indicated for large memberships).
entra.hasgroups: Indicates group overage where full group list is not included in token.
entra.uti: Unique token identifier used for internal correlation.
entra.xms_cc: Client capability claim used for specific platform features.
entra.xms_cae: Continuous Access Evaluation related claim metadata.

auth0.scope: Space-separated scopes granted to the client for this access token.
auth0.permissions: Permissions granted to the token, present when the Auth0 API enables RBAC with permissions in the access token.
auth0.gty: Grant type used to obtain this token, for example client-credentials or authorization_code.
auth0.client_id: Client ID the token was issued to, typically present on client credentials tokens.
auth0.org_id: Auth0 organization identifier when the user signed in through an organization.
auth0.org_name: Auth0 organization name when the user signed in through an organization.
auth0.azp: Authorized party: the client the token was issued to.

settings.flowIntro: High-level overview of the Authorization Code + PKCE flow.
settings.flowDiagram:
Client (Browser)
   |
   | 1) Generate code_verifier + code_challenge (S256)
   v
Authorize Endpoint ------------------------------>
   |   GET .../authorize?client_id=...&redirect_uri=...
   |        &response_type=code&scope=...&state=...
   |        &code_challenge=...&code_challenge_method=S256
   |
   | 2) User signs in and consents
   v
Redirect (Callback) <------------------------------
   |   http(s)://your-app/callback/auth-code?code=...&state=...
   |
   | 3) Exchange code for tokens with code_verifier
   v
Token Endpoint ----------------------------------->
   |   POST grant_type=authorization_code
   |        &client_id=...
   |        &code=...
   |        &redirect_uri=...
   |        &code_verifier=...
   |
   | 4) Receive tokens (access_token, id_token, ... )
   v
Protected API (e.g., Graph) --------------------->
   |   Authorization: Bearer <access_token>
   v
  Response

StepAuthentication.description: Choose how the client will authenticate to the token endpoint when exchanging the authorization code.

help.clientAuthMethod: Choose how the client authenticates to the token endpoint when exchanging the code.
help.clientSecret: Your confidential client secret. For demo purposes this value stays in memory only (not persisted).
help.privateKeyPem: Keep this secure! This private key is used to sign the client assertion JWT.
help.publicKeyPem: The public key corresponding to your private key.
help.certificatePem: Upload this certificate or public key material to your identity provider's client credentials or signing keys configuration.
help.thumbprintSha1: Use this as the Key ID (kid) when your provider identifies uploaded certificates by thumbprint.
help.clientAssertionKid: This should match the key identifier configured for the client signing key at your identity provider.
help.assertionClaims: Preview of the JWT claims that will be used in the client_assertion parameter.
help.testAssertion: A test client_assertion JWT generated with your private key.
help.decodedAssertion: The decoded header and payload of the test JWT for verification purposes.
help.auth0ClientAssertionKid: Auth0 derives this from the JWK thumbprint of your public key when the credential is created. The dashboard does not display it — read it from the Management API response for the credential.

placeholders.publicKeyPem: Generated automatically with the private key
placeholders.certificatePem: Click "Generate Certificate" to create a self-signed certificate
placeholders.assertionClaims: Click "Preview Claims" to see the JWT claims
placeholders.testAssertion: Click "Generate Test Assertion" to create a test JWT
placeholders.decodedAssertion: Generated automatically when test assertion is created

generateKeyPair.title: Step 1: Generate RSA Key Pair
generateKeyPair.description: Generate a 2048-bit RSA key pair for signing the client assertion JWT.

generateCertificate.title: Step 2: Create Self-Signed Certificate
generateCertificate.description: Create a self-signed X.509 certificate to upload to your identity provider. The certificate thumbprint can be used as the kid.

configureKid.title: Step 3: Key ID (kid) - Auto-populated
configureKid.description: The certificate thumbprint (SHA-1) is automatically used as the Key ID. Some providers display the same value as a certificate thumbprint.

previewClaims.title: Step 4: Preview Client Assertion Claims
previewClaims.description: Preview the JWT claims that will be used in the client_assertion parameter.

testAssertion.title: Step 5: Test Generate Signed Assertion
testAssertion.description: Generate a test client_assertion JWT to verify it's working. The actual assertion will be created when calling the token endpoint.

auth0RegisterPublicKey.title: Step 2: Register the public key with Auth0
auth0RegisterPublicKey.description: Copy the public key above into your application's Credentials tab, under Private Key JWT, with signing algorithm RS256. Auth0 stores the public key itself — no certificate is involved, so there is no thumbprint to compute here.

auth0ConfigureKid.title: Step 3: Key ID (kid) - from the Auth0 credential
auth0ConfigureKid.description: Auth0 generates the key ID when it stores the credential, so it has to be read back rather than derived. Paste it here to identify which credential signed the assertion.

note.label: Note:
note.body: Due to browser limitations, secrets must be sent to the server, where the token endpoint call is actually made.

errors.keyPairRequired: Please generate a key pair first.
errors.certificateUnreadable: This does not read as a certificate PEM, so no thumbprint could be derived. Paste the certificate itself — the block beginning -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- — rather than a private key or a truncated copy.
errors.missingKid: Please enter or generate a Key ID first.
errors.missingClientConfig: Please configure client ID and token endpoint first.
errors.missingKeyOrConfig: Please generate a key pair and configure settings first.

overview.flowIntro: High-level overview of the Authorization Code + PKCE flow for public clients (no client secret).
overview.flowDiagram:
Client (SPA)
   |
   | 1) Generate code_verifier + code_challenge (S256)
   v
Authorize Endpoint ------------------------------>
   |   GET .../authorize?client_id=...&redirect_uri=...
   |        &response_type=code&scope=...&state=...
   |        &code_challenge=...&code_challenge_method=S256
   |
   | 2) User signs in and consents
   v
Redirect (Callback) <------------------------------
   |   https://app/callback?code=...&state=...
   |
   | 3) Exchange code for tokens (no client secret)
   v
Token Endpoint ----------------------------------->
   |   POST grant_type=authorization_code
   |        &client_id=...
   |        &code=...
   |        &redirect_uri=...
   |        &code_verifier=...
   |
   | 4) Receive tokens (access_token, id_token, ... )
   v
Protected API (e.g., Graph) --------------------->
   |   Authorization: Bearer <access_token>
   v
  Response

overview.flowIntro: High-level overview of the Authorization Code flow for confidential clients (with client authentication).
overview.flowDiagram:
Client (Web/App)
   |
   | 1) (Optional) Generate code_verifier + code_challenge (PKCE)
   v
Authorize Endpoint ------------------------------>
   |   GET .../authorize?client_id=...&redirect_uri=...
   |        &response_type=code&scope=...&state=...
   |        &code_challenge=...&code_challenge_method=S256
   |
   | 2) User signs in and consents
   v
Redirect (Callback) <------------------------------
   |   https://app/callback?code=...&state=...
   |
   | 3) Exchange code for tokens with client auth
   v
Token Endpoint ----------------------------------->
   |   POST grant_type=authorization_code
   |        &client_id=...
   |        &code=...
   |        &redirect_uri=...
   |        &client_secret=... OR client_assertion=...
   |        &code_verifier=... (if PKCE)
   |
   | 4) Receive tokens (access_token, id_token, ... )
   v
Protected API (e.g., Graph) --------------------->
   |   Authorization: Bearer <access_token>
   v
  Response
